newsitem.title: USA: US FERC upholds most of its open power grid rules.
newsitem.headline: US FERC upholds most of its open power grid rules.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday reaffirmed the core elements of its open access rules for the nation's power grid.

The commission rejected calls for a revision of its policy on the recovery of stranded costs for utilities that lose customers in the competitive market, in its review of the sweeping transmission rules it issued last April.
However, the commission made some minor changes including asserting authority over the recovery of stranded costs for municipal utilities that expand their customer territory.
FERC also modified its rules to require that utilities offering discounts for transmission space must offer the discounts on their electronic bulletin board.
"We are definitely encouraged by the implementation of 888 (the open access rules) to date," said Commissioner Vicky Bailey.

In its review the commission made clear that it would make sure that power producers and marketers would have access to retail markets in states that had opened the electricity business to competition.
"The commission will not tolerate ... attempts to block access," Commissioner Donald Santa said at the commission's meeting Wednesday.

Two commissioners, William Massey and James Hoecker, dissented from part of the order, saying that the commission should not second guess states' decisions on the recovery of stranded costs by municipal utilities.
